objects.name: dark cliff across the top left
objects.note: NEVER animate

objects.name: thatched pavilion at the top
objects.note: ruled lines -- rigid, never deforms

objects.name: thatched hall at the top left
objects.note: ruled architectural lines. A building NEVER deforms -- any wobble in it destroys the whole illusion, so it must sit rigid on its own plane

objects.name: ridge across the top right
objects.note: the far plane the conifer rows sit on

objects.name: teal canopy along the top edge
objects.note: clipped by the top edge

objects.name: band of teal and ochre trees along the top
objects.note: several overlapping crowns on the upper shelf; cut apart before hinging

objects.name: teal and ochre trees at the top right corner
objects.note: the scroll's right margin

objects.name: teal pine on the upper ridge
objects.note: clean separated clusters despite the distance

objects.name: orange-red maple in the top left
objects.note: clipped; continues into the tile to the right

objects.name: cliff mass behind the hall
objects.note: NEVER animate

objects.name: two figures at the hall and its gate
objects.note: small; robe hems only, and at this size probably leave still

objects.name: rust tree beside the upper pavilion
objects.note: sits against the building -- must not drag the roofline

objects.name: ochre and rust hanging-leaf tree upper left
objects.note: drooping strokes -- flutter reads better than swing

objects.name: teal round-leaf tree on the upper left ledge
objects.note: clean separated clusters on a pale branch

objects.name: pink and rust tree beside the hall
objects.note: sits directly against the building -- must not drag the roofline with it

objects.name: dark hanging-leaf tree below the pavilion
objects.note: drooping strokes; flutter rather than swing

objects.name: cluster of dark conifers on the far ridge
objects.note: distant silhouettes -- leave still

objects.name: dark wall the fall drops through
objects.note: the dark frame that makes the white ribbon read; must stay rigid or the fall appears to swing

objects.name: hatched water channel down the right side
objects.note: horizontal hatching IS the water surface here -- the strokes are the ripples, so they move as a surface, not as cards

objects.name: the enormous bare cliff filling the tile
objects.note: the largest continuous bare passage in the whole zone -- NEVER animate, and the strongest clean-plate donor available anywhere in z3w

objects.name: second figure at the hall door
objects.note: only the robe hem moves

objects.name: the waterfall dropping between dark walls
objects.note: combed white stripes on bare silk -- NEGATIVE SPACE, there is no ink here to cut into cards. It moves as a surface. The brightest and most legible water in the zone

objects.name: paling fence below the hall
objects.note: ruled lines -- rigid

objects.name: the great rock mass through the centre
objects.note: NEVER animate; the conifer rows sit on its shoulders

objects.name: needle pine on the right cliff shoulder
objects.note: small feathered fans hanging over the drop

objects.name: big orange-rust maple down the left edge
objects.note: clipped by the left edge; the strongest colour mass in the tile

objects.name: row of spiky dark conifers climbing the centre ridge
objects.note: distant silhouette marks -- leave still. A hinge at this size is jitter, not wind

objects.name: teal round-leaf tree on the left ledge
objects.note: clean separated clusters

objects.name: rust brick-mark tree in the centre
objects.note: leaves drawn as short horizontal dashes in tight rows -- the same grammar as t010's bottom thicket

objects.name: grove of slim teal trees on the left terrace
objects.note: several thin trunks with small crowns; rig as a group, small swing

objects.name: tall slim conifers on the right bank
objects.note: big enough to read; narrow crowns, so a small swing about a high pivot

objects.name: teal round-leaf tree below and right of it
objects.note: overlaps the brick tree; cut the crowns apart before hinging or they swing as one slab

objects.name: scattered conifers below that row
objects.note: distant marks -- leave still

objects.name: pale slope running down from the fall
objects.note: bare wash

objects.name: the pool and spill below the fall
objects.note: where the ribbon breaks up; slower than the drop above it

objects.name: row of dark conifers on the left slope
objects.note: distant silhouette marks -- leave still

objects.name: the broad pale slope through the middle
objects.note: nearly bare silk; a good clean-plate donor

objects.name: row of small dark conifers across the mid left
objects.note: DISTANT MARKS, not trees. At this size a hinge produces visible jitter and no readable motion -- leave still. This is the class that made canopy-by-texture-statistics fail

objects.name: ochre, rust and teal grove at the lower left
objects.note: several crowns of different colour and grammar packed together -- cut them apart before hinging. This grove stands directly behind Ge Hong

objects.name: grove of teal and rust trees across the bottom right
objects.note: the nearest foliage in the tile and the largest leaf marks; several distinct crowns on ochre trunks

objects.name: bare forked sapling below the slope
objects.note: NO LEAVES -- nothing to cut cards from

objects.name: teal tree at the bottom centre
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: railed bridge at the lower right
objects.note: ruled lines; rigid like the hall

objects.name: teal tree at the bottom right corner
objects.note: the scroll's right margin at the bottom

objects.name: red-orange cluster tree at the bottom left
objects.note: the largest leaf marks in the tile; clipped by both edges

objects.name: 白衣 white-robed figure with black cap on the path, bottom left
objects.note: THIS IS GE HONG, the subject of 葛稚川移居圖. The largest and most legible figure in the zone. Robe hem and sleeve only -- the body must not deform, and nothing else in frame may draw the eye off him

objects.name: bare saplings over ochre foliage, bottom centre
objects.note: bare forks above a low ochre crown; the forks have no leaves to cut

objects.name: stream at the bottom centre by the figure
objects.note: the near water; Ge Hong stands at its edge

objects.name: teal tree at the bottom centre
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: ochre hanging-leaf tree in the top left corner
objects.note: long vertical drooping strokes; flutter, not swing -- continues into t006

objects.name: big ochre and rust hanging-leaf tree on the ridge
objects.note: the dominant living form in this tile; drooping strokes hang BELOW their branch, so the hinge line sits along the top of the mass

objects.name: dark gorge wall on the left
objects.note: frames the fall

objects.name: figures on the stepped path at the top
objects.note: the travelling party; robes and hems are the only moving parts

objects.name: big grey ridge across the top right
objects.note: broad wash, no leaf marks

objects.name: cliff shoulder the upper trees stand on
objects.note: the pale mass at the top left

objects.name: small teal tree on the upper ledge
objects.note: on the shoulder above; leaves visible but small

objects.name: pale peak rising behind the ridge trees
objects.note: nearly bare silk; a parallax plane boundary, not a subject

objects.name: teal and ochre canopy at the right edge
objects.note: clipped; continues into the tile to the right

objects.name: teal pine cluster below the maple
objects.note: dot-cluster leaves on pale ochre branches

objects.name: teal dot-cluster pine below the ochre tree
objects.note: the cleanest separated crown in the tile

objects.name: bright unpainted gap between the shoulders
objects.note: 留白 -- bare silk reading as air, not mist ink (knowledge/mist-as-ink.md)

objects.name: narrow fall dropping through the left gorge
objects.note: white 留白 between two dark rock walls, not painted ink

objects.name: tall grey cliff face on the right
objects.note: vertical wash strokes, no colour; THIS is the graphite the leaf cards must never swallow

objects.name: red-orange autumn maple
objects.note: the colour accent of the tile; sits against the cliff face, does NOT include the cliff

objects.name: teal tree leaning right off the upper ledge
objects.note: long bare branch reaching right; canopy is the left half only

objects.name: streaked wet rock down the left edge
objects.note: vertical drip strokes are texture, not water

objects.name: streaked wet cliff face on the left
objects.note: vertical drip strokes read as texture, not as water

objects.name: the domed cliff mass filling the whole lower two thirds
objects.note: graphite 牛毛皴 over broad wash -- NEVER animate; this is the surface earlier colour gates kept fusing into canopy cards

objects.name: old blue-green pine spreading left over the ledge
objects.note: biggest tree in the tile; trunk drawn in dry brush, leaf clusters clearly separated

objects.name: blue-green pine cluster mid-tile
objects.note: two or three crowns overlapping, leaves individually drawn

objects.name: round-leaf teal tree mid-tile
objects.note: clean separated leaf marks, good hinge candidate

objects.name: orange-red maple on the cliff shoulder
objects.note: the colour accent; sits AGAINST the cliff and must not take the cliff with it

objects.name: teal canopy at the right edge
objects.note: continues into the tile to the right -- merge across the overlap

objects.name: blue-green needle pine lower left
objects.note: needle fans, not dot clusters; the widest sprays in the tile

objects.name: cliff face filling the right half
objects.note: graphite 牛毛皴 texture strokes -- NEVER animate

objects.name: ochre-yellow tree below the red maple
objects.note: smaller leaf marks than the pines

objects.name: pale rounded boulder mass below the pines
objects.note: the trees stand on this; it reads as one rounded form

objects.name: round-leaf tree below the pine
objects.note: overlaps the pine above it; crowns must be cut apart before hinging

objects.name: teal tree at the lower right
objects.note: cut by the tile edge

objects.name: teal foreground canopy at the bottom left
objects.note: largest leaf marks in the tile; clipped by both the left and bottom edges

objects.name: foreground canopy along the bottom edge
objects.note: clipped by the tile edge; continues into the tile below

objects.name: teal crown entering from below
objects.note: small round clusters, well separated from the wall behind

objects.name: cliff wall down the whole left edge
objects.note: NEVER animate

objects.name: big teal round-leaf tree spreading across the top left
objects.note: the dominant tree of the tile; leaf clusters clearly separated from pale ochre branches -- an ideal hinge subject. Canopy ONLY; its trunk is a separate object

objects.name: dark cliff mass across the top left
objects.note: NEVER animate

objects.name: upper crown of the same broadleaf, top right corner
objects.note: clipped by the top edge; continues into t005 above -- expect a seam merge

objects.name: broadleaf crown reaching in from the top left
objects.note: the same great broadleaf as t009's; clipped -- expect a seam merge to the left

objects.name: the great pale boulder filling the tile
objects.note: the largest bare rock passage in z3w -- NEVER animate, and the single best clean-plate donor in the zone

objects.name: the cliff wall behind everything
objects.note: the backdrop plane the trees sit in front of

objects.name: waterfall dropping down the centre right
objects.note: three white 留白 stripes between dark rock edges -- there is NO ink to animate here, this is negative space and must be moved as water, not as strokes

objects.name: pale vertical streaks down the centre of the wall
objects.note: reads as a thin distant fall or seepage over the cliff. Faint -- if it will not carry motion, leave it still rather than inventing a stream

objects.name: bare ochre branch curling below that crown
objects.note: a leafless limb. It is the HINGE LINE for the crown above it, not a card of its own

objects.name: the great broadleaf tree filling the right half
objects.note: the single biggest living form in the zone; each leaf is drawn as its own outlined mark on ochre branches. Sprays hang off long limbs and this is where a hinge rig should read best. Cut it into several cards along its branches, not one

objects.name: small ochre tree on the left ledge
objects.note: clipped by the left edge

objects.name: the dark trunk descending from that tree
objects.note: a trunk does NOT move; it is the anchor the canopy hinges above. Cataloguing it separately is what stops a colour gate fusing trunk into card

objects.name: pale cliff face behind the trunk
objects.note: the flattest passage in the tile; a good clean-plate donor

objects.name: rust and pink dot-cluster tree on the left ledge
objects.note: the colour accent; pale pink ring-marks. Very close in tone to the rock it sits on -- this is the exact case a colour gate gets wrong

objects.name: blue-green needle pine on the right ledge
objects.note: flat needle fans on ochre branches; sprays hang off a nearly horizontal limb, so swing reads strongly here

objects.name: two red collector seals on the cliff
objects.note: vermilion seal impressions sit ON the silk, not IN the scene. They must never enter a card, a plane, or a colour gate -- red is exactly what a maple gate looks for

objects.name: pale bare slope across the lower left
objects.note: nearly bare silk; the best clean-plate donor in this tile

objects.name: dark wedge of rock at the lower left
objects.note: the darkest rock in the tile; tonally identical to leaf ink, which is why tone alone cannot separate them

objects.name: small red passage among the pines at the bottom right
objects.note: UNCERTAIN at this resolution -- a red-robed figure or autumn colour, the same ambiguity as t014's red-mark-top-right. Read at full scale before rigging either way

objects.name: dark needle pines across the bottom right
objects.note: fine needle fans, the darkest foliage here; a different grammar from the thicket beside it and must not share its card style

objects.name: bare forked sapling above the thicket
objects.note: NO LEAVES -- nothing to cut cards from

objects.name: exposed ochre roots at the left edge
objects.note: roots and trunks do not move

objects.name: brick-dash canopy band across the top
objects.note: leaves as short horizontal dashes in tight rows over pale ochre limbs. Densest ink in the tile; the marks are small, so leaf-mark seed spacing must come from the ink and not from a neighbour tile

objects.name: cliff wall on the right
objects.note: the pine's roots grip this -- share its depth plane

objects.name: cliff mass down the left
objects.note: NEVER animate

objects.name: pale ledge running across the top left
objects.note: bare silk; the far plane

objects.name: pale rock down the left edge
objects.note: the only substantial bare passage in the tile, and therefore the only clean-plate donor -- a thin one

objects.name: red passage inside the canopy at the top right
objects.note: UNCERTAIN, and the LARGEST of the three red passages in the zone (see t014 and t011). Either a red-robed figure deep in the trees or a maple in autumn colour. Read at full scale before rigging -- a figure wants a robe cycle, a maple wants leaf cards, and guessing wrong is visible

objects.name: bare ochre roots spread across the clifftop
objects.note: an anchor, never a card. Catalogued separately precisely because it is ochre and lies on pale rock -- a colour gate reads it as leaf

objects.name: the broad stream running through the middle
objects.note: bare silk with fine RIPPLE LINES curling around each rock. The lines ARE the water -- they move as a surface, never as cards. The widest water passage in z3w and the strongest argument that this zone needs water motion, not only foliage

objects.name: the scatter of dark rocks standing in the water
objects.note: each is ringed by its own ripple lines -- the rocks stay put and the rings move around them. Animating these is the exact defect Ryan called out

objects.name: the blunt cliff head filling the centre
objects.note: NEVER animate. Broad flat wash with sparse contour -- a strong clean-plate donor

objects.name: tangle of bare ochre limbs through the upper left
objects.note: hinge lines, not cards. Ochre on pale ground -- exactly what a colour gate mistakes for leaf

objects.name: brick-dash canopy through the centre
objects.note: continues the band above; cut along the limbs that divide them

objects.name: dark needle pine at the right edge
objects.note: the scroll's right margin

objects.name: wall of teal foliage down the right edge
objects.note: many overlapping crowns rather than one tree; must be cut into cards along its branches or it swings as a slab

objects.name: teal round-leaf tree at the left
objects.note: clipped by the left edge; the clearest separated crown in the tile

objects.name: the big round-leaf tree through the centre
objects.note: larger, better separated marks than the brick band -- an easier hinge

objects.name: dense round-leaf mass filling the bottom right
objects.note: many crowns fused into one field. As a single card this is a slab; it only reads once split into leaf marks

objects.name: pale valley floor glimpsed at the left edge
objects.note: 留白 -- bare ground read as distance. There is no ink here to move; see refuted claim mist-as-ink

objects.name: bare limbs below the left canopy
objects.note: the hinge lines for the crowns above and below. Ochre on pale ground -- a colour gate reads this as leaf, which is why it is catalogued

objects.name: two figures at the left edge
objects.note: clipped by the left edge; one carries a bundle

objects.name: child sitting between two bird cages
objects.note: the most charming passage in the zone and a natural station. Robe and hem only -- the face must NOT deform, and the cages are ruled structures that stay rigid

objects.name: teal tree with red-tipped leaves at the lower left
objects.note: the clearest leaf drawing in the tile -- outlined lobed leaves in loose sprays on ochre limbs. An ideal hinge subject

objects.name: lobed-leaf tree reaching in from the right
objects.note: the ONLY real foliage in the tile; red-tipped lobed leaves in loose sprays on an ochre limb -- clean, well separated, an easy hinge subject

objects.name: dense round-leaf mass across the bottom right
objects.note: many crowns fused into one field of ink. The clearest case in z3w of a mass that must be split into leaf marks -- as one card it is a slab

objects.name: feathered blue-green fronds at the bottom left
objects.note: long feathered sprays rather than clusters; these hang off their stem, so the hinge sits at the stem end and flutter carries more than swing

objects.name: teal tree at the bottom right
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: robed gentleman holding a fan, bottom right
objects.note: the largest figure in the tile; wide sleeves and a long hem, so the robe carries real motion

objects.name: bare forked sapling at the bottom centre right
objects.note: NO LEAVES -- nothing to cut cards from; whole-twig sway or nothing

objects.name: denser canopy below it, clipped by the bottom edge
objects.note: continues below the tile

objects.name: porter with a shoulder basket
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge; the load is rigid, the robe is not

objects.name: figure with a covered load at the bottom centre
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge
